reviewed_version: arXiv:2312.01715v2, 18 April 2025, 44 pages; journal-final equivalence not assumed
paper_title: Interlacing Polynomial Method for Matrix Approximation via Generalized Column and Row Selection
summary: One Major coefficient-extraction defect makes the specified expected-polynomial computation incorrect; four Minor normalization/domain issues have explicit repairs. The correctly defined interlacing existence theorem is not refuted.

problems.title: A.16 selects the wrong coefficient of y
problems.location: AppendixA.6, equations(A.14)–(A.16), pp.37–38; computation cited in Lemma4.2 and Algorithm1
problems.check: g=(x+z)(x+y-1)(x+y-4). Direct definition gives P=2x^2-5x; literal A.16 uses mu_(j,c1,rhat) and yields -5x^2+4x. Correct index khat yields 2x^2-5x.
problems.result: The printed coefficient extraction is not equal to the expected polynomial. Wrong maximum root 4/5 is below minimum feasible residual squared norm 1; true maximum root is 5/2.
problems.counterevidence: The correct determinant formula (3.5b) and abstract definition remain valid in the example. This is not an Algorithm1 full-trajectory counterexample or a refutation of Theorem1.1.
problems.impact: A central supplied polynomial-computation/certificate route fails. Wrong degree coefficient changes roots, not just harmless normalization.
problems.correction: Replace every mu_(j,c1,rhat) remaining after the y derivative in A.16 by mu_(j,c1,khat).
problems.correction_verification: Exact general coefficient selection follows from partial_y^khat at y=0; tested equality against definition and (3.5b) in six further rank-deficient-source configurations.

problems.title: Filter zero projected directions before normalization
problems.check: Line3 visits index2 and requests q2=0/0 before Line5 excludes zero directions.
problems.result: Literal pseudocode is undefined on an explicitly admissible input.
problems.counterevidence: Lemma4.1 already defines the correct nonzero candidate set W; its mathematical argument does not normalize zero vectors.
problems.impact: Local domain guard omission; no contradiction to rank-preserving selection or corrected algorithmic guarantee.
problems.correction: Restrict candidate preparation and polynomial evaluation to Qb_i!=0 and Pc_i!=0 before normalizing. The rank assumptions ensure enough admissible directions until the target size is reached.
problems.correction_verification: Analytic span/rank argument and explicit exact zero-column example.

problems.title: LemmaA.2 places the factorial on the wrong side
problems.location: LemmaA.2 p.35 and its use immediately below
problems.check: Sum of size1 characteristic polynomials is 3x-6. Printed LHS is 3x/2-3 while characteristic second derivative is 6x-12.
problems.result: The displayed identity is false for k=2.
problems.counterevidence: The subsequent proof of Proposition3.5 uses sum=(1/k!) derivative, which is the correct normalization; positive global factors do not change roots.
problems.impact: Local displayed normalization error; no demonstrated damage to Proposition3.5 or Theorem1.4.
problems.correction: Use sum_(|S|=d-k) det(xI-M_SS)=(1/k!) partial_x^k det(xI-M), equivalently move k! to multiply the sum.
problems.correction_verification: Exact polynomial computation; differentiation counts k! deletion orders.

problems.title: The projected-zero target leaves alpha undefined
problems.check: U^T A A^T U=0, so the normalization defining alpha is 0/0 even with nonzero A.
problems.result: Parameter definition is not defined on all matrices introduced by the statement.
problems.counterevidence: BB^dagger A=0 makes every selected-column residual equal A; the desired bound is trivial there.
problems.impact: Missing degenerate-case convention, not a false nondegenerate reconstruction inequality.
problems.correction: Handle BB^dagger A=0 separately; define alpha only when its denominator is positive.

problems.title: The Laguerre root lemma needs a nonconstant degree range
problems.location: Lemma6.1 p.27; proof p.28; application p.29
problems.check: k>beta*d/(1+beta)=2/3 but (partial_x x partial_x)^2 p=4, whose largest root is undefined. At k=3 the polynomial is zero and the printed radical is not real.
problems.result: The stated unrestricted positive-integer k range overreaches its defined root expression.
problems.counterevidence: Theorem1.4 uses deletion order d-k with positive retained k, hence at most d-1; this example does not refute its bound.
problems.correction: State beta*d/(1+beta)<k<d, or separately define and handle degree-exhaustion cases. Treat beta=0 minimization at b=1 by a one-sided limit.
problems.correction_verification: Exact degree-lowering calculation; checked downstream range conversion.
